Calculation aid. Results depend on your inputs and the assumptions shown. They are not a design approval, a compliance check or a certificate. You are responsible for checking them against the standards and rules that apply to your installation, the manufacturer's data and the network operator's requirements.

Inputs

SystemSingle-phase AC (1~)
Voltage230 V
Current16 A
Length18 m
Conductor materialcopper
Cross-section1.5 mm²
cos φ1
Limit3 %

Assumptions

  • Power factor cos φ = 1
  • L is the one-way cable length
  • Annex G constants for copper: ρ1 = 0.0225 Ω·mm²/m, reactance λ = 0.00008 Ω/m (used when no cable data is known)
  • Selected limit 3 % (custom limit)
  • Standard sizes checked: IEC 60228 series 0.5 to 300 mm²
  • The smallest size comes from the selected voltage-drop limit alone: current-carrying capacity Iz, overload and short-circuit protection and disconnection are not checked here (use Protection coordination and Loop impedance)
  • Method comparison uses θ = 70 °C (M2), κ = 56 m/(Ω·mm²) (M3), X' = 0.00008 Ω/m (default)

Working

  1. ρ1 = 0.0225 Ω·mm²/m (Annex G, includes the operating-temperature allowance)
  2. R = ρ × L / S = 0.0225 Ω·mm²/m × 18 m / 1.5 mm² = 0.27 Ω
  3. sin φ = √(1 − cos² φ) = √(1 − 1²) = 0
  4. u = b × (R × cos φ + X'/n × L × sin φ) × I = 2 × (0.27 Ω × 1 + 0.00008 Ω/m × 18 m × 0) × 16 A = 8.64 V
  5. Δu = 100 × u / U0 = 100 × 8.64 V / 230 V = 3.76 %
  6. U_end = U − u = 230 V − 8.64 V = 221.36 V
  7. P_loss = 2 × I² × R = 2 × 16 A² × 0.27 Ω = 138.24 W
  8. L_max = limit × U0 / (100 × b × I × (ρ/S_eff × cos φ + X'/n × sin φ)) = 3 % × 230 V / (100 × 2 × 16 A × (0.0225 Ω·mm²/m / 1.5 mm² × 1 + 0.00008 Ω/m × 0)) = 14.3 m
  9. Smallest standard size with Δu ≤ 3 %: 2.5 mm² (Δu = 2.26 %)
  10. Next smaller size 1.5 mm²: Δu = 3.76 %, above 3 %
  11. M2 physics at conductor temperature: Δu = 3.45 %
  12. M3 fixed conductivity κ: Δu = 2.99 %
